services.name: Convex
services.does: Hosts turtl's backend, database, and file storage
receives: Everything turtl stores

services.name: OpenAI
services.does: Names the parts of the code, diagnoses a problem, proposes fixes, answers questions, sorts customers' reports, and turns speech into text and text into speech
receives: Excerpts of source code
Case details
Messages
Notes and preferences the owner writes
Customers' reports
Voice recordings

services.name: Supermemory
services.does: Finds the code and the past cases that matter to a question or a new problem
receives: Up to 30,000 characters of each source file
Notes on past cases
Preferences the owner states
Questions about the code
Customers' reports

services.name: Capy
services.does: Writes an approved code change, or the changes that prepare a new project, and opens a pull request
receives: The title of a case
The instructions for an approved code change
The brief for preparing a new project: its name, folders, live address, and what turtl found missing
The repository's name
The repository itself, through Capy's own connection to GitHub

services.name: GitHub
services.does: Signs the owner in when they choose GitHub, holds the repositories turtl reads through its GitHub App, and the pull requests it follows and merges
receives: The owner's approval when they sign in with GitHub or connect it, and requests to read who they are and which repositories they chose
Requests to read those repositories and their pull requests
A check that the owner can still change a repository, before a merge or a code change
A merge, when the owner taps Merge
A request to remove turtl's GitHub App when the owner disconnects GitHub or deletes their account

services.name: Revyl
services.does: Runs the owner's app on a phone in its cloud to check a fix, and sends back screenshots
receives: The id of the test to run

services.name: Expo
services.does: Delivers push notifications to the owner's phone, through Apple
receives: The phone's push token, sent by the phone when the owner turns notifications on
Each notification: the project's name, one fixed sentence, and the case's id

services.name: Resend
services.does: Sends the email that confirms a new password account's address, and the password reset email
receives: The owner's email address
A one-time code (to confirm the address, or to reset the password)

services.name: Apple
services.does: Signs the owner in when they choose Sign in with Apple, and revokes that sign-in when they delete their account
receives: Apple's one-time code from the sign-in, traded for a token turtl keeps only to revoke it
That token, when the owner deletes their account

services.name: The owner's own app
services.does: Answers turtl's health checks and carries out an approved recovery
receives: Health checks and the approved recovery action, with the project's control token (in the single-owner demo, the deployment's control secret)

otherHosts.ronoktanvir.github.io: turtl's own privacy, terms, and support pages, opened in the browser from the gear sheet
otherHosts.app.invalid: A placeholder address in a prompt. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.example.invalid: A placeholder address in developer sample data. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.api.anthropic.com: Anthropic's model API. The council can ask it for a second diagnosis when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, but only in the single-owner demo: with accounts on, the AI permission refuses every call to it, because this list does not name it
otherHosts.generativelanguage.googleapis.com: Google's Gemini API. The council can ask it for a second diagnosis when GEMINI_API_KEY is set, but only in the single-owner demo: with accounts on, the AI permission refuses every call to it, because this list does not name it
otherHosts.127.0.0.1: The demo's own app on a local backend, and stand-ins in tests. With accounts on, a project's live address may not be one
otherHosts.docs.expo.dev: A link to Expo's documentation in a comment. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.invalid.example: A placeholder the backend reads when it has no address of its own. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.your-deployment.convex.site: A placeholder in the GitHub App's definition, replaced with the backend's own address when the app is registered. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.example.com: An example address in a message to the owner. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.app.example.com: An example address in a message to the owner. Nothing is sent to it
otherHosts.guardian-scoring.vercel.app: The live address of a project in the app's example data, shown as a link. The app sends nothing to it
otherHosts.orca-teams.vercel.app: The live address of a project in the app's example data, shown as a link. The app sends nothing to it
otherHosts.onkeiki.com: Keiki, which texts the owner of the single-owner demo when a case needs them. Only in that demo: its one phone number reads as unset with accounts on, and the AI permission refuses every call to it, because this list does not name it

otherSettings.VOICE_ENABLED: Switches talking on. Off by default
otherSettings.CODE_NETWORK_CHAT_ENABLED: Switches questions about the code on. Off by default
otherSettings.ASSISTANT_ENABLED: Switches the unused assistant function on. Keep it off
otherSettings.DEV_TOOLS_ENABLED: Switches the backend's developer tools on. Never set in production
otherSettings.EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_TOOLS: Shows the developer tools in the app. Never set in a store build
otherSettings.EXPO_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE: Set to example, the app shows example data and calls no backend
otherSettings.EXPO_PUBLIC_TURTL_INTAKE_URL: The demo app's report form: where it posts reports
otherSettings.EXPO_PUBLIC_TURTL_INTAKE_KEY: The demo app's report form: which app the report is for
otherSettings.TURTL_PREVIEW_ORIGIN: The address of a web preview, used when building one
otherSettings.AUTH_REQUIRED: Unset, empty or false: the single-owner demo, which makes no accounts and refuses to run on a backend that holds any. Any other value: accounts mode, with sign-in, one owner per project, the AI permission and the limits
otherSettings.SITE_URL: turtl's web address, where GitHub sign-in may return
otherSettings.CONVEX_CLOUD_URL: The backend's own address, set by Convex. Used to tell a local backend from a hosted one
otherSettings.CONVEX_SITE_URL: The backend's own web address, set by Convex. Sign-in tokens name it, GitHub sends the owner back to it, and the monitor asks it, with no token and no body, whether turtl's own requests get out before a not-answering case opens
otherSettings.AUTH_STAND_IN_URL: Points sign-in at a stand-in for Apple, GitHub and Resend in tests. With accounts on it is honoured only on a local backend
otherSettings.SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY: Encrypts each project's control token and each account's coding agent key. Never sent anywhere
otherSettings.INTAKE_CONTACT_KEY: The key for the hash a customer's contact on the report form becomes. The contact itself is not kept
otherSettings.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: Lets the council ask Anthropic, in the single-owner demo only (see api.anthropic.com)
otherSettings.GEMINI_API_KEY: Lets the council ask Google, in the single-owner demo only (see generativelanguage.googleapis.com)
otherSettings.MODEL_SPEND_LIMIT_USD: The AI spend one account may reach in a month
otherSettings.CODING_THREADS_PER_DAY: The code changes one account may start in a day
otherSettings.INTAKE_SPEND_PER_DAY_USD: The AI spend one project's customer reports may use in a day
otherSettings.INTAKE_CASES_PER_DAY: The cases customer reports may open on one project in a day
otherSettings.NEW_ACCOUNTS_PER_HOUR: The new accounts made with Apple or GitHub in an hour
otherSettings.NEW_ACCOUNTS_PER_DAY: The new accounts made with Apple or GitHub in a day
otherSettings.DEPLOYMENT_MODEL_SPEND_PER_DAY_USD: The AI spend of every account together in a day
otherSettings.PROJECTS_PER_ACCOUNT: The projects one account may have
otherSettings.INTAKE_KEYS_PER_PROJECT: The report form keys one project may have at once
otherSettings.EVIDENCE_LOCAL_PROOF: Opens the local evidence fixtures on a local backend. Never set in production
otherSettings.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV: Which kind of build this is. Picks Apple's development or production push service
otherSettings.KEIKI_API_KEY: Lets the single-owner demo text its owner through Keiki (see onkeiki.com)
otherSettings.KEIKI_AGENT_ID: The Keiki agent the single-owner demo texts through
otherSettings.KEIKI_OWNER_CONTACT: The one phone number the single-owner demo texts. Read as unset with accounts on
otherSettings.KEIKI_BASE_URL: Points Keiki calls at a stand-in in tests. With accounts on it is honoured only on a local backend
otherSettings.PRACTICE_BREAKS_PER_DAY: How many times one account may break its practice app in a day. A number; it sends nothing anywhere
otherSettings.PASSWORD_SIGNUPS_PER_HOUR: The password sign-ups the backend accepts in an hour, before any address is confirmed
otherSettings.PASSWORD_SIGNUPS_PER_DAY: The password sign-ups the backend accepts in a day. With at most five emails each, it bounds a day's confirmation emails
otherSettings.CONFIRMED_SIGNUPS_PER_HOUR: The password accounts that may confirm their address in an hour
otherSettings.CONFIRMED_SIGNUPS_PER_DAY: The password accounts that may confirm their address in a day
otherSettings.ACCOUNT_MODEL_SPEND_PER_DAY_USD: The AI spend one account may use in a day
otherSettings.ACCOUNT_INTAKE_SPEND_PER_DAY_USD: The AI spend one account's customer reports may use in a day
otherSettings.OUTAGE_RESERVE_PERCENT: The share of the backend's daily AI ceiling kept for finding the cause of outages
otherSettings.OUTAGE_RESERVE_ACCOUNT_USD: Only an account that has spent less than this today may draw on that reserve
otherSettings.EMAILS_PER_DAY: The most emails the backend sends in a day, all kinds together, apart from each confirmed address's first reset of the day. Set it below the email plan
otherSettings.CUSTOM_AUTH_SITE_URL: The backend's own web address on a custom domain, where GitHub sign-in starts. Also refused as a project's live address
otherSettings.OUTAGE_RESERVE_STEADY_HOURS: How long a project's check must have passed before it failed for its case to draw on the outage reserve
otherSettings.OUTAGE_RESERVE_ACCOUNT_AGE_DAYS: How old an account must be for its outages to draw on the outage reserve
otherSettings.PRACTICE_AI_PER_DAY_USD: The part of an account's daily AI share its practice app's cases may use
otherSettings.OUTAGE_FLOOR_PER_DAY_USD: The AI spend each account keeps every day for finding the cause of an outage on its own project, which no other account can use up
otherSettings.DEPLOYMENT_MODEL_HARD_STOP_PER_DAY_USD: The most the backend spends on AI in a day, every account and every floor together. Unset, twice the daily ceiling

libraries.@auth/core: Sign in with GitHub, used only in the backend
libraries.@convex-dev/auth: Sign-in and sessions, in turtl's own backend
libraries.@expo-google-fonts/capriola: The font, shipped inside the app. No request to Google
libraries.@expo-google-fonts/righteous: The second font, shipped inside the app. No request to Google
libraries.convex: The client for turtl's own backend
libraries.expo-apple-authentication: Shows Apple's own Sign in with Apple sheet
libraries.expo-asset: Loads files that ship inside the app
libraries.expo-audio: Records and plays audio after the owner taps Talk
libraries.expo-crypto: Makes the one-time value a Sign in with Apple request carries
libraries.expo-file-system: Reads the recording and deletes it; writes and deletes the spoken reply
libraries.expo-notifications: Asks to show notifications after the owner taps Turn on notifications, and gets the phone's push token from Expo
libraries.expo-secure-store: Keeps the owner passcode in the iOS Keychain
libraries.expo-web-browser: Opens GitHub's sign-in page in a browser sheet
libraries.jose: Checks Apple's sign-in tokens and signs turtl's requests to Apple, used only in the backend
libraries.lucia: Hashes passwords (Scrypt), used only in the backend
libraries.react-dom: The UI library, for the web preview
libraries.react-native-svg: Draws icons and the map of the code
libraries.supermemory: The client for Supermemory, used only in the backend
